sections.title: Foundations (Stages 4–5)
sections.description: Core living things, energy, materials, light and space ideas from Stages 4 and 5.

questions.question: Which part is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.options: the cell wall | the cell membrane | the cytoplasm | the nucleus
questions.explanation: Only plant cells have a stiff cell wall around the outside to hold their shape. Membrane, nucleus and cytoplasm are in both kinds of cell.

questions.question: In which part of a cell is energy released from food?
questions.options: the nucleus | the mitochondria | the vacuole | the chloroplast
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the tiny power stations of the cell. The chloroplast makes food in plants, the vacuole stores sap and the nucleus is the control centre.

questions.question: A red blood cell has no nucleus and is shaped like a flat disc. Which job is it specialised for?
questions.options: carrying oxygen around the body | carrying nerve messages | making food by photosynthesis | taking in water from the soil
questions.explanation: Losing the nucleus leaves more room for the red pigment that grabs oxygen, and the flat disc shape gives a big surface for oxygen to move across.

questions.question: In which state of matter are the particles close together but still able to slide past each other?
questions.options: a gas | a liquid | a solution | a solid
questions.explanation: In a liquid the particles still touch but they can slip and slide, which is why a liquid pours and takes the shape of its container.

questions.question: Which of these substances is an element?
questions.options: brass | sea water | oxygen | water
questions.explanation: An element is made of only one kind of atom, and oxygen is one kind of atom. Water is a compound, while brass and sea water are mixtures.

questions.question: What happens to the temperature of a block of ice while it is melting?
questions.options: It rises and then falls | It falls steadily | It stays the same | It rises steadily
questions.explanation: While ice melts, all the heat energy going in is used to break the particles apart, so the temperature holds still at 0 °C until the melting is finished.

questions.question: A bag of rice has a mass of 6 kg. On Earth, where g = 10 N/kg, what is its weight?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × g, so 6 kg × 10 N/kg = 60 N. Mass is measured in kilograms, but weight is a force measured in newtons.

questions.question: An astronaut travels from Earth to the Moon. Which statement is true?
questions.options: Her mass stays the same but her weight becomes less | Her mass and her weight both become greater | Her mass and her weight both stay the same | Her weight stays the same but her mass becomes less
questions.correctAnswer: Her mass stays the same but her weight becomes less
questions.explanation: Mass is how much stuff you are made of, so it never changes. Weight is the pull of gravity, and the Moon pulls more gently than Earth does.

questions.question: Which of these animals is an invertebrate?
questions.options: a snail | an ostrich | a shark | a frog
questions.explanation: Invertebrates have no backbone, and a snail has none. Frogs, ostriches and sharks all have a backbone, so they are vertebrates.

questions.question: Halima is building a dichotomous key for the beetles in her garden. Which question works best in her key?
questions.options: Do you like this beetle? | Does it have spots on its wing cases? | Is it quite a big beetle? | Is it a pretty beetle?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it have spots on its wing cases?
questions.explanation: A key question must have a clear yes or no answer that everyone would agree on. Pretty, quite big and do you like it all depend on opinion.

questions.question: Which property means a material can be hammered into thin sheets without breaking?
questions.options: malleable | ductile | brittle | magnetic
questions.explanation: Malleable materials can be hammered flat. Ductile means it can be pulled into wires, and brittle means it snaps instead.

questions.question: A liquid turns red litmus paper blue. What kind of liquid is it?
questions.options: alkaline | neutral | acidic | an indicator
questions.explanation: Red litmus turning blue is the sign of an alkali. An acid would turn blue litmus red, and a neutral liquid would leave the paper unchanged.

questions.question: Yusuf has a jar of salty water. Which method gets the salt back as a dry solid?
questions.options: pouring it through a sieve | evaporating the water away | filtering the mixture | holding a magnet over it
questions.explanation: The salt has dissolved, so it slips straight through filter paper and a sieve. Letting the water evaporate leaves the salt crystals behind.

questions.question: What must always happen before a sound can be made?
questions.options: something must dissolve | something must get hot | something must glow | something must vibrate
questions.explanation: Every sound starts with a vibration, whether it is a drum skin, a guitar string or your own vocal cords shaking to and fro.

questions.question: Through which of these can sound NOT travel?
questions.options: water | steel | air | empty space
questions.explanation: Sound needs particles to pass its vibrations along. Empty space has no particles, so no sound can cross it — space really is silent.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth lies directly below the crust?
questions.options: the mantle | the outer core | the atmosphere | the inner core
questions.explanation: Going inwards the order is crust, mantle, outer core, inner core. The atmosphere is the blanket of air above the crust, not below it.

questions.question: Which two groups of living things do most of the decomposing in nature?
questions.options: fish and birds | lizards and frogs | grasses and trees | bacteria and fungi
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi break dead material down into nutrients that go back into the soil, which is why nothing dead piles up forever.

questions.question: In the food chain grass → goat → lion, what name is given to the goat?
questions.options: a primary consumer | a top predator | a producer | a decomposer
questions.explanation: The goat is the first animal to eat, so it is the primary consumer. The grass is the producer and the lion is the top predator here.

questions.question: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.options: ice melting | water boiling | wood burning | sugar dissolving in tea
questions.explanation: Burning makes brand new substances such as ash and carbon dioxide, and you cannot get the wood back. The other three can all be reversed.

questions.question: An iron gate rusts when it is left in contact with which two things?
questions.options: nitrogen and oil | oxygen and water | carbon and salt | hydrogen and sand
questions.explanation: Rusting is iron slowly reacting with the oxygen in air while water is present. Paint or oil keeps both away and stops the rust.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the current flowing in a circuit?
questions.options: a thermometer | a voltmeter | a balance | an ammeter
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures current in amps and is joined into the circuit so the current flows through it. A voltmeter measures voltage instead.

questions.question: In a simple series circuit, adding a second cell and changing nothing else makes the current:
questions.options: unchanged | smaller | zero | larger
questions.explanation: Two cells push the charges round harder than one, so more current flows and the lamp glows more brightly.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood all around your body?
questions.options: the kidneys | the heart | the stomach | the lungs
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscle that squeezes over and over, pushing blood through your blood vessels day and night.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: Why does your heart rate go up while you are running?
questions.options: Your muscles need more oxygen, so blood must be delivered faster | Your blood becomes heavier and harder to move | Your lungs stop working while you run | Your heart is trying to cool your body down
questions.correctAnswer: Your muscles need more oxygen, so blood must be delivered faster
questions.explanation: Working muscles burn more food to release energy, and that needs extra oxygen. A faster heartbeat delivers oxygen-rich blood more quickly.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: A desert plant stores water inside a thick fleshy stem. What is this an example of?
questions.options: a decomposer | an adaptation | a food chain | a habitat
questions.explanation: An adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive where it lives. A thick water-storing stem suits a place with very little rain.

questions.question: Which of these changes is reversible?
questions.options: baking a cake | melting chocolate | rusting a nail | burning paper
questions.explanation: Melted chocolate turns solid again when it cools, so nothing new was made. Baking, burning and rusting all make new substances for good.

questions.question: Sugar is stirred into warm water until it can no longer be seen. What has happened to the sugar?
questions.options: It has disappeared completely | It has melted into a gas | It has dissolved to make a solution | It has turned into water
questions.correctAnswer: It has dissolved to make a solution
questions.explanation: The sugar is still there, spread out as tiny particles between the water particles. Taste the water and you will find it.

questions.question: When the forces acting on a moving object are unbalanced, the object will:
questions.options: change its speed or its direction | become heavier | keep moving in exactly the same way | stop existing
questions.correctAnswer: change its speed or its direction
questions.explanation: Unbalanced forces always change motion — speeding up, slowing down or turning. Balanced forces leave the motion just as it was.

questions.question: Amina is testing how far a toy car rolls across three different surfaces. What should she do to keep the test fair?
questions.options: Use a different car on each surface | Push harder on the rough surface | Measure the distance only once | Release the car from the same height every time
questions.correctAnswer: Release the car from the same height every time
questions.explanation: In a fair test only one thing changes — here, the surface. Everything else, including the starting height, must stay exactly the same.

questions.question: Which of these materials is the best electrical conductor?
questions.options: rubber | dry wood | copper | plastic
questions.explanation: Copper lets electricity flow through it easily, which is why wires are made of it. Plastic, wood and rubber are insulators that block the flow.

questions.question: Which group of vertebrates has feathers and lays eggs?
questions.options: reptiles | amphibians | birds | mammals
questions.explanation: Feathers belong to birds alone. Mammals have hair and feed their young milk, while reptiles have scales and amphibians have moist skin.

questions.question: Ismail’s family fits solar panels on the roof. Why is sunlight called a renewable energy source?
questions.options: It formed deep underground millions of years ago | It gives off more smoke than coal does | It can be burned only once and is then gone | It keeps arriving every day and will never run out
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps arriving every day and will never run out
questions.explanation: Renewable sources refill themselves, and the Sun shines on us every single day. Coal, oil and gas took millions of years to form and are being used up.

questions.question: A torch bulb lights up only when:
questions.options: the circuit makes a complete loop with no gaps | the wires are made of plastic | the switch is left open | the cell is taken out
questions.correctAnswer: the circuit makes a complete loop with no gaps
questions.explanation: Electricity needs an unbroken path from one end of the cell, through the bulb, and back again. A single gap stops the whole circuit.

questions.question: Which three things does a seed need in order to germinate?
questions.options: sunlight, salt and sand | wind, ice and rock | water, warmth and air | soil, sugar and shade
questions.explanation: A seed carries its own food store, so it only needs water, warmth and air to wake up. Light matters later, once the leaves appear.

questions.question: Washing on a line dries fastest on a day that is:
questions.options: cold and cloudy | cold and still | warm and windy | cool and damp
questions.explanation: Heat gives water particles the energy to escape, and wind carries the damp air away, so evaporation happens much faster.

questions.question: How long does the Earth take to travel once all the way around the Sun?
questions.options: one month | one year | one week | one day
questions.explanation: One full orbit of the Sun takes about 365 days, and that journey is what we call a year. One spin on its axis makes a day.
